newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond volatilities soft, August fades.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond volatilities soft, August fades.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were softer as underlying bond prices slipped after briefly edging up to fresh highs, dealers said.
August T-bond futures options, which expire on Friday, came under intense pressure as strong buying interest in 115 calls in the past few days faded.
With only one more day to trade, a pullback in September futures away from the 115 level quickly turned the 115 calls from at-the-money to low-delta options, traders noted.
"August is pretty much off the books," said a bank affiliate trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
A Wall Street firm was said to have sold a total of 6,000 contracts of August 115 calls.
On Wednesday, open interest in the contract ballooned by 13,253 contracts to 29,544 after the high-gamma option came in demand as September futures rallied toward the strike price.
Short-dated options have higher gamma, which provides quicker premium acceleration against movement in the underlying instrument, but are vulnerable to time decay.
Time decay also weighed on September volatilities, traders said.

With most economic data for the week out of the way and Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony not due until next Tuesday, market makers were beginning to take out the weekend time-decay, they said.
Implied volatility for September T-bond futures options fell about 0.15 point to about 7.9 percent.
In Eurodollar futures options, volatilities were genrally flat, with December at about 9.4 percent.
December futures briefly rose to the 94.090 high touched twice last week but failed to break through, fueling anticipation of further range-bound trading near term, a brokerage trader said.
